Definition: from G746 and a compound of G5140 and G2827 (a dinner-bed, because composed of three couches); director of the entertainment:--governor (ruler) of the feast.
BiblicalUsage: The word is the governor of the feast, the master of the banquet, and it appears at Cana, when Jesus tells the servants to draw out the water made wine and bear it to the governor, who tastes it and calls the bridegroom.
TheologicalSignificance: The governor of the feast did not know where the good wine came from, but the servants did, and that is often how a miracle works.
